steps.sevenths: Stack one more third on a triad and you get a seventh chord, with four notes. Three are the most common: {g7}, a major triad with a minor seventh, called a dominant seventh; {cMaj7}, a major triad with a major seventh; and {dMin7}, a minor triad with a minor seventh.
steps.onKeys: Name the chord: first the triad, then the seventh on top of it.
steps.build: Now play them: all four notes, in any order.
steps.restless: Each one has its own color: the major seventh is soft and dreamy, the minor seventh is mellow, and the dominant seventh, like {g7}, is restless. It wants to move on. The next unit shows why.
steps.ear: Now with your ears. Listen for the restless one first.
